5 to 7 months covers a full remodel from first conversation to final walkthrough. A cosmetic refresh (new countertops, hardware, paint, and lighting) can move faster. Removing walls or relocating plumbing and electrical puts you toward the longer end.

We start with an initial consultation about your goals, priorities, and general budget range, then a site visit to assess your space and any structural constraints. Early renderings show you what’s possible before anything is decided. This is also where your overall timeline comes into focus.

Showroom visits are one of our favorite parts. Seeing materials in person, side by side and in different light, makes all the difference. Quick deciders move faster, and if you’re still exploring, that’s completely fine. Better to land it here than change course after cabinets are ordered.

- Placing orders for every selection
- Finalizing permits, if required
- Confirming delivery windows

White Birch Design is a full-service design/build/remodeling company specializing in kitchen, bath & basement design and remodel projects. We know what it takes to create a space that a homeowner has always dreamed of. We also understand that our clients are putting their homes in our hands. Placing a priority on dependable and positive communication, we strive to build a relationship with our clients based on accountability, honesty, and respect.

Here at White Birch Design, we pride ourselves on offering many of the ‘perks’ of the larger design/build companies without the big price tag and impersonal communication. Our ‘boutique’ like approach to kitchen, bath and basement remodeling is affordable and specialized. We offer high-quality work and excellent customer service with a personal approach, inviting homeowners to feel a part of the process and valued as a customer.

White Birch Design is based in Lakeville, MN. While our primary focus is kitchen, bath & basement remodeling in the South Metro communities of Lakeville, Eagan, Apple Valley, Burnsville, Rosemount, Prior Lake and Savage, we also work with homeowners across the Minneapolis and St. Paul area.

How long does a kitchen remodel actually take? 🏡

For a full remodel, plan on 5 to 7 months from the first conversation to the final walkthrough. 

About half of that time happens before demo day, and that planning is what keeps construction on track.

Swipe through the five phases to see what each one involves and how long it takes. 👉

Thinking about a kitchen project in 2027? Now is the perfect time to start the design conversation. Planning something smaller? We still have a few openings left this year.

📌 Save this for when you’re ready to plan, and reach out through the link in bio. No start date or final design needed, just a conversation.

#WhiteBirchDesign #KitchenRemodel #RemodelingTips #designbuildmn 

5 to 7 months covers a full remodel from first conversation to final walkthrough. A cosmetic refresh (new countertops, hardware, paint, and lighting) can move faster. Removing walls or relocating plumbing and electrical puts you toward the longer end.

We start with an initial consultation about your goals, priorities, and general budget range, then a site visit to assess your space and any structural constraints. Early renderings show you what’s possible before anything is decided. This is also where your overall timeline comes into focus.

Showroom visits are one of our favorite parts. Seeing materials in person, side by side and in different light, makes all the difference. Quick deciders move faster, and if you’re still exploring, that’s completely fine. Better to land it here than change course after cabinets are ordered.

Once your contract is signed, we start ordering your selections, many from local Minnesota vendors. Behind the scenes, we’re:
- Placing orders for every selection
- Finalizing permits, if required
- Confirming delivery windows

Many homes built in the ‘90s have closed-off kitchens, half walls, and separate dining rooms, so opening them up often takes structural work. Once walls open, we sometimes find outdated electrical or off-code plumbing. We plan for those surprises and tell you right away when one comes up. Tip: most homeowners set up a temporary kitchen in another room.

Our Values

Here at White Birch Design, we pride ourselves on offering many of the ‘perks’ of the larger design/build companies (experienced design and project management) without the big price tag and impersonal communication.

Our boutique like approach to kitchen, bath and basement remodeling is affordable and specialized. We offer high-quality work and excellent customer service with a personal approach, inviting homeowners to feel a part of the process and valued as a customer.

Our company was founded on principles which we are committed to upholding in every home transformation we undertake.

INTEGRITY

Accountable, trustworthy, honest, fair, and respectful

QUALITY

Quality materials and quality work

CRAFTSMANSHIP

Attention to detail, experienced team, pride in what we do

RELATIONSHIPS

Dependable and positive communication, value our relationship with clients throughout project and after

COMMUNITY

We prioritize supporting the communities we work in through philanthropic efforts with organizations like the Ronald McDonald house

We pride ourselves on creating spaces people love to live in, all while keeping within a budget, designing with quality, and executing with local, experienced craftsmen that

share our values and outlook.

CO-OWNERS, STEVE MCDONALD AND ANGELA BARNHART, HAVE A COMBINED 30+ YEARS IN THE DESIGN, CONSTRUCTION, AND REAL ESTATE INDUSTRIES.

Bringing this unique combination of experience into each and every project, we guide homeowners through the entire process, from concept to design to construction, to transform their kitchen, bath or lower level space into something they love while also understanding the best options to

maximize their return on investment.

Two stages of remodeling over two years, and now it feels like home. 🤍

Foundry main floor remodel, Lakeville, MN.

#WhiteBirchDesign #LakevilleMN #MainFloorRemodel #KitchenRemodel #MinnesotaHomes

How long does a kitchen remodel actually take? 🏡

For a full remodel, plan on 5 to 7 months from the first conversation to the final walkthrough. 

About half of that time happens before demo day, and that planning is what keeps construction on track.

Swipe through the five phases to see what each one involves and how long it takes. 👉

Thinking about a kitchen project in 2027? Now is the perfect time to start the design conversation. Planning something smaller? We still have a few openings left this year.

📌 Save this for when you’re ready to plan, and reach out through the link in bio. No start date or final design needed, just a conversation.

#WhiteBirchDesign #KitchenRemodel #RemodelingTips #designbuildmn 

5 to 7 months covers a full remodel from first conversation to final walkthrough. A cosmetic refresh (new countertops, hardware, paint, and lighting) can move faster. Removing walls or relocating plumbing and electrical puts you toward the longer end.

We start with an initial consultation about your goals, priorities, and general budget range, then a site visit to assess your space and any structural constraints. Early renderings show you what’s possible before anything is decided. This is also where your overall timeline comes into focus.

Showroom visits are one of our favorite parts. Seeing materials in person, side by side and in different light, makes all the difference. Quick deciders move faster, and if you’re still exploring, that’s completely fine. Better to land it here than change course after cabinets are ordered.

Once your contract is signed, we start ordering your selections, many from local Minnesota vendors. Behind the scenes, we’re:
- Placing orders for every selection
- Finalizing permits, if required
- Confirming delivery windows

Many homes built in the ‘90s have closed-off kitchens, half walls, and separate dining rooms, so opening them up often takes structural work. Once walls open, we sometimes find outdated electrical or off-code plumbing. We plan for those surprises and tell you right away when one comes up. Tip: most homeowners set up a temporary kitchen in another room.

The punch list is a detailed walkthrough of everyth

Designed for a family that gathers often, with a main floor that has a place for everyone. 

The character comes from the details. 

Here are nine from this Lakeville main floor remodel: 
1. A stone fireplace up to the existing soffit, under 18-foot ceilings 
2. White oak built-ins in a Sandalwood stain, with champagne bronze hardware 
3. A custom iron railing from a local ironworker 
4. Tambour on the dining room walls, with sconces 
5. A Tambour wall in the piano room 
6. Tambour on the back of the island, with a Zellige tile backsplash 
7. A custom arched hutch 
8. A powder room gone dark, with wood-textured tile 
9. A cabinet that hides the printer 

Save this one for your own main floor, and see the full project at the link in bio under Kitchen.

#MainFloorRemodel #twincitiesremodeler #LakevilleMN #mndesignbuild #whitebirchdesign 

Start here: a stone fireplace that climbs to the existing soffit under 18-foot ceilings, right at the center of the floor.

White oak built-ins in a Sandalwood stain and champagne bronze hardware bring warmth to all that stone.

The stairs got a custom iron railing from a local ironworker, and the carpet carries right up beside it.

Take out the soffits and columns, and the dining room opens right up. A Tambour detail brings the texture.

Right across from the dining room, the piano room picks up the same Tambour detail, with sconces on the wall.

Look closely. The Tambour detail follows you into the kitchen on the back of the island, and a Zellige tile backsplash adds more texture.

The custom arched hutch gives this kitchen even more personality.

Then a surprise: the powder room goes dark, with wood-textured tile.

Even the office got a plan: a custom white oak desk and a cabinet that hides the printer. 

Which room is your favorite?

We’re not saying a new kitchen fixes everything. 👀 

We’re just saying nobody has ever been sad about warm white oak cabinets and a custom hood. 🙌 

Fun fact: that hood was finished by a local artisan in a custom color and texture, and it gives the whole room its character. 

First peek at our Foundry Kitchen remodel. Ready to start yours? DM us and let’s talk. 

#WhiteBirchDesign #KitchenRemodel #SouthMetroMN #MNDesignBuild

Behind every finished kitchen photo is a lot of nudging, fussing, and “wait, one more inch to the left.” 😄 

Swipe through our latest photo shoot to see what goes into capturing a space the way it deserves: 

🕯️ Finding the perfect placement 
🍏 A little pop of green before the shutter clicks 
📷 Getting every angle just right 
👯 A crew that makes it fun 

The details you live with every day, like the cabinetry, the lighting, and the way a room flows, deserve to be seen properly. That’s why we take the photos as seriously as the build. 

The final reveal is coming soon. 

Thinking about a kitchen, bath, or basement remodel? DM us or tap the link in our bio and let’s talk. 

#WhiteBirchDesign #KitchenRemodel #mndesignbuild #twincitiesremodeler

A choppy layout and a few partial walls were boxing in this Lakeville, MN kitchen. Once they came down, it got the room it was always meant to have:

🤍 An island scaled for real life
🤍 A built-in beverage center made for hosting
🤍 Hickory floors running through the whole main level, so it all reads as one space

Missed us, or living with a layout that feels chopped up? Tell us what’s not working. Link in bio to get started.

How long does a kitchen remodel actually take? 🏡

For a full remodel, plan on 5 to 7 months from the first conversation to the final walkthrough. 

About half of that time happens before demo day, and that planning is what keeps construction on track.

Swipe through the five phases to see what each one involves and how long it takes. 👉

Thinking about a kitchen project in 2027? Now is the perfect time to start the design conversation. Planning something smaller? We still have a few openings left this year.

📌 Save this for when you’re ready to plan, and reach out through the link in bio. No start date or final design needed, just a conversation.

#WhiteBirchDesign #KitchenRemodel #RemodelingTips #designbuildmn 

5 to 7 months covers a full remodel from first conversation to final walkthrough. A cosmetic refresh (new countertops, hardware, paint, and lighting) can move faster. Removing walls or relocating plumbing and electrical puts you toward the longer end.

We start with an initial consultation about your goals, priorities, and general budget range, then a site visit to assess your space and any structural constraints. Early renderings show you what’s possible before anything is decided. This is also where your overall timeline comes into focus.

Showroom visits are one of our favorite parts. Seeing materials in person, side by side and in different light, makes all the difference. Quick deciders move faster, and if you’re still exploring, that’s completely fine. Better to land it here than change course after cabinets are ordered.

Once your contract is signed, we start ordering your selections, many from local Minnesota vendors. Behind the scenes, we’re:
- Placing orders for every selection
- Finalizing permits, if required
- Confirming delivery windows

Many homes built in the ‘90s have closed-off kitchens, half walls, and separate dining rooms, so opening them up often takes structural work. Once walls open, we sometimes find outdated electrical or off-code plumbing. We plan for those surprises and tell you right away when one comes up. Tip: most homeowners set up a temporary kitchen in another room.

Designed for a family that gathers often, with a main floor that has a place for everyone. 

The character comes from the details. 

Here are nine from this Lakeville main floor remodel: 
1. A stone fireplace up to the existing soffit, under 18-foot ceilings 
2. White oak built-ins in a Sandalwood stain, with champagne bronze hardware 
3. A custom iron railing from a local ironworker 
4. Tambour on the dining room walls, with sconces 
5. A Tambour wall in the piano room 
6. Tambour on the back of the island, with a Zellige tile backsplash 
7. A custom arched hutch 
8. A powder room gone dark, with wood-textured tile 
9. A cabinet that hides the printer 

Save this one for your own main floor, and see the full project at the link in bio under Kitchen.

#MainFloorRemodel #twincitiesremodeler #LakevilleMN #mndesignbuild #whitebirchdesign 

Start here: a stone fireplace that climbs to the existing soffit under 18-foot ceilings, right at the center of the floor.

White oak built-ins in a Sandalwood stain and champagne bronze hardware bring warmth to all that stone.

The stairs got a custom iron railing from a local ironworker, and the carpet carries right up beside it.

Take out the soffits and columns, and the dining room opens right up. A Tambour detail brings the texture.

Right across from the dining room, the piano room picks up the same Tambour detail, with sconces on the wall.

Look closely. The Tambour detail follows you into the kitchen on the back of the island, and a Zellige tile backsplash adds more texture.

The custom arched hutch gives this kitchen even more personality.

Then a surprise: the powder room goes dark, with wood-textured tile.

Even the office got a plan: a custom white oak desk and a cabinet that hides the printer. 

Which room is your favorite?

We’re not saying a new kitchen fixes everything. 👀 

We’re just saying nobody has ever been sad about warm white oak cabinets and a custom hood. 🙌 

Fun fact: that hood was finished by a local artisan in a custom color and texture, and it gives the whole room its character.

The details you live with every day, like the cabinetry, the lighting, and the way a room flows, deserve to be seen properly. That’s why we take the photos as seriously as the build.

EAGAN, MN  |  2026

Fleur Primary Bath Remodel
This primary bath remodel was an opportunity to completely rethink the space and create a retreat that feels as beautiful as it is functional.

The original bathroom felt closed in and inefficient, with a large corner tub taking up valuable space, a cramped shower, and a layout that didn’t provide the privacy or ease the homeowners needed. Through the remodel, we reworked the space with a focus on openness, function, and a more elevated sense of comfort.

A soft, layered color palette brings warmth and depth to the room, balancing deeper cabinetry tones with lighter walls and natural-feeling finishes. Subtle pattern and texture add dimension throughout, while the herringbone tile detail introduces a timeless element and a touch of visual interest.

Every detail was thoughtfully considered to create a space that feels calm, cohesive, and inviting. The result is a primary bath that not only functions beautifully for everyday living, but also feels like a private retreat designed for comfort and relaxation.

The Nineteenth Hole Primary Bath Remodel

LAKEVILLE, MN  |  2025

Sometimes inspiration shows up in the most unexpected places,
and that's exactly what happened here. A glimpse of Cambria Clovelly in a golf course clubhouse bathroom planted a seed, and a decade-long wish for a primary bath that finally felt personal gave it room to grow.

The original bathroom was dominated by a jetted tub nobody used, a shower that felt undersized, and a layout that lacked privacy and storage. The tub is gone now, replaced by a spacious walk-in shower with a built-in bench and frameless glass enclosure. A dedicated makeup station, better storage, and a reconfigured layout give the space a flow it never had. Meanwhile, seamless aging in place features like shower grab bars, encourage longevity.

The design move that made it all come together was an unconventional one: placing the vanity directly in front of the existing window. Suspended illuminated mirrors and light fixtures hang in front of the glass, preserving views of the outdoors while flooding the space with both natural daylight and warm interior lighting.

As the original source of inspiration, it’s only appropriate that Cambria Clovelly runs throughout, countertops, shower bench, curb, and niche, anchored by rich cherry cabinetry with a dark oak stained finish that ties the bathroom seamlessly to the adjoining suite. Meanwhile, champagne bronze fixtures and textured tile walls add warmth and depth at every turn. The result is a striking, contemporary space that feels personal and completely worth the wait.
